# IDataverseConnectionPool

- Namespace/type: `PPDS.Dataverse.Pooling.IDataverseConnectionPool`
- Assembly: `PPDS.Dataverse`

## Summary

Manages a pool of Dataverse connections with intelligent selection and lifecycle management. Supports multiple connection sources for load distribution across Application Users.

#### GetTotalRecommendedParallelism

```text
public System.Int32 GetTotalRecommendedParallelism()
```

Gets the total recommended parallelism across all connection sources. This is the sum of live RecommendedDegreesOfParallelism for each source.


Returns: The total recommended parallelism across all sources.

Remarks: The value comes from the x-ms-dop-hint response header, exposed via ServiceClient.RecommendedDegreesOfParallelism. This is Microsoft&#x27;s recommended concurrent request limit per Application User. This reads live values from seed clients, not cached values, so it reflects the server&#x27;s current recommendation which may change based on load.

#### EnsureInitializedAsync

```text
public System.Threading.Tasks.Task EnsureInitializedAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
```

Ensures the pool is initialized by warming all seed connections. Triggers authentication and DOP discovery. Idempotent - subsequent calls are no-ops.

- Parameter `cancellationToken`: Cancellation token.

Returns: A task that completes when initialization is done.

#### ExecuteAsync

```text
public System.Threading.Tasks.Task`1<Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk.OrganizationResponse> ExecuteAsync(Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk.OrganizationRequest request, System.Threading.CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
```

Executes a request with automatic retry on service protection errors. This is a convenience method that handles connection management and throttle retry internally. The caller doesn&#x27;t need to handle service protection exceptions - they are handled transparently.

- Parameter `request`: The organization request to execute.
- Parameter `cancellationToken`: Cancellation token.

Returns: The organization response.

Remarks: This method will: 1. Get a healthy (non-throttled) connection from the pool 2. Execute the request 3. If throttled, automatically wait and retry with a different connection 4. Return the successful response Service protection errors never escape this method - it retries until success or cancellation.

#### InvalidateSeed

```text
public System.Void InvalidateSeed(System.String connectionName)
```

Invalidates the seed client for a connection, forcing fresh authentication on next use.

- Parameter `connectionName`: The name of the connection source to invalidate.

Remarks: Call this when a token failure is detected (e.g., MessageSecurityException with &quot;Anonymous&quot;). This removes the cached seed client so the next connection request will create a fresh seed with a new authentication token. This is different from marking individual pooled connections as invalid. When a token expires, all clones of the seed share the same broken authentication context. Simply disposing pool members doesn&#x27;t help - new clones from the same seed will also fail. Invalidating the seed forces a complete re-authentication.

### Properties

#### BatchCoordinator

```text
PPDS.Dataverse.BulkOperations.BatchParallelismCoordinator BatchCoordinator { get; }
```

Gets the batch parallelism coordinator for coordinating concurrent bulk operations.


Remarks: Use this coordinator to ensure that concurrent bulk operations (e.g., multiple entities importing in parallel) don&#x27;t exceed the pool&#x27;s total capacity. Each batch should acquire a slot from the coordinator before execution. The coordinator tracks the pool&#x27;s live DOP and adjusts capacity dynamically as the server&#x27;s recommendation changes (e.g., during throttle recovery).

#### InitializationResults

```text
System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList`1<PPDS.Dataverse.Pooling.SeedInitializationResult> InitializationResults { get; }
```

Gets the results of seed initialization for each connection source.


Remarks: Use this to check whether all connection sources initialized successfully. A source may fail to initialize due to invalid credentials, network issues, etc. Failed sources will use a default DOP of 4 and may fail on first actual request. Check this property after pool construction to detect configuration issues early.

#### SourceCount

```text
System.Int32 SourceCount { get; }
```

Gets the number of connection sources configured in the pool. This represents the number of Application Users/app registrations available.
